To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of finite-width sparse networks is primarily determined by their initialization and the distance of their kernel to that of a wide, dense, infinite-width network.

1) for sparse, randomly-initialized neural networks, model width is more important than the number of weights, and 2) the performance of a finite width, sparsely-initialized model is correlated with the distance between its Gaussian process kernel and the kernel of its infinite width counterpart.

(i) for models initialized with random, static sparsities, the performance of finite-width networks is largely independent of the number of parameters as long as training accuracy is achieved, and (ii) the performance of such networks can be predicted by the distance between the finite- and infinite-width kernels at initialization.

the effect of width on the performance of deep neural networks.

the number of parameters in a neural network is a poor proxy for model capacity.
the width of a model, rather than the number of parameters, is the determining factor of performance, at least in the case of random, static sparsities.
